final_candidates.decision_summary: A charged substitution in the C-terminal BRCT region is predicted to strongly impair BRCA1 DNA-repair function while retaining the rest of the full-length protein.
This nonconservative substitution in the BRCT domain is likely to disrupt critical functional interactions through a localized change.
Introducing a negatively charged residue at this BRCT-domain position is likely to perturb domain function without deleting the overall protein.

stop_reason.detail: The leading three candidates are already well prioritized for localized BRCT-domain loss of function, and no external evidence is available to refine the ranking.

history.rationale: R1699 lies in the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding domain, and replacing the conserved charged residue with bulky tryptophan is likely to disrupt BRCT-mediated interactions while retaining a folded domain.
Retain as a high-priority BRCT-domain disruption candidate with a plausible localized effect on BRCA1 function.
A1708 is a structurally constrained BRCT-domain residue; introducing a negatively charged glutamate is expected to perturb the domain interaction surface and abolish repair activity.
Retain because introducing a charged residue at this BRCT-domain position is likely to perturb functional interactions without requiring a truncation.
M1775 is central to the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding interface, and substitution by arginine should strongly disrupt ligand recognition without directly removing the domain.
Retain as a strong candidate because it targets the BRCT region while a single substitution is compatible with preserving the rest of the protein.
The glycine at 1788 occupies a constrained BRCT structural position; valine may impair local packing and phosphopeptide-dependent function while being less globally disruptive than truncation.
Retain as a plausible structural and functional perturbation in the C-terminal BRCT region, though with lower confidence than the leading candidates.

Y1853 is near the C-terminal BRCT domain boundary and contributes to the structured terminal region; cysteine substitution may impair BRCT stability or interactions while preserving most of the protein.
Retain as a distal BRCT-domain candidate that may impair DNA-repair activity while remaining a single-residue substitution.
